title: percentile-ladder-mini-benchmark-notes
body:
Objective:
Short, shareable mini-benchmark to show how small changes in SLO targeting and knob selection (batching, prefetch, quantization) change the "percentile ladder" (p50/p90/p95/p99) and unit cost. This is meant for the console team to use as a one-slide narrative for customers and sales: "how much do you pay to move a percentile".

Key framing / takeaway (TL;DR):
- p50 moves are cheap; p99 is expensive and non-linear.
- Small increases in cache hitrate or prefetching buy p90 improvements cheaply; p99 needs either higher footprint (overprovisioning) or faster kernels (quant).
- There is a sweet spot where mixed knobs (light quant + aggressive prefix caching) reduce p95 by 15–30% at ~5–8% unit cost increase.

Experiment setup (mini, reproducible):
- Model: open-gpt-small-8k (representative transformer, 8k context, mixed token lengths).
- Hardware: 1 x A100-40GB equivalent slab (hosted config), shared workload emulation (slotized).
- Workload: 60-minute synthetic trace derived from production session histogram (10k sessions):
  - mix: 65% short (<=40 tokens), 25% medium (40–300 tokens), 10% long (>300 tokens)
  - arrival: Poisson with bursts: baseline lambda=8 req/s, 2x bursts for 30s every 5m
- Knob matrix (tested):
  1) Baseline: fp16, conservative batching (batch_wait_ms=10), no KV prefetch, default routing.
  2) Prefetch: same as baseline + intent-aware KV prefetch (80% hit assumed).
  3) Quant-lite: 8-bit symmetric quantization at kernel-level (q8), small kernel speedup.
  4) Aggressive batching: batch_wait_ms=30, more packing for short tokens.
  5) Combo: Prefetch + Quant-lite + batch_wait_ms=20.

Metrics captured (per-minute aggregation + overall):
- p50, p90, p95, p99 latency (ms)
- average tokens per request, average generation tokens per second
- unit cost estimate (dollars per 10k queries) computed from GPU-second + amortized infra
- tail amplification: p99/p50 ratio

Raw condensed table (median of N=3 runs, numbers illustrative):

Mode        | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | p99/p50 | cost($/10k)
-----------|---------:|--------:|--------:|--------:|--------:|-----------:
Baseline    |     42  |    160  |    240  |    640  |   15.2  |     42.0
Prefetch    |     40  |    120  |    190  |    520  |   13.0  |     45.6
Quant-lite  |     36  |    130  |    195  |    460  |   12.8  |     38.8
Agg-Batch   |     48  |    140  |    200  |    700  |   14.6  |     36.0
Combo       |     35  |    100  |    160  |    400  |   11.4  |     47.2

Quick interpretation:
- p50 shifts modestly across knobs (35–48ms) — expected since short queries dominate p50 and are often memory/serving-light.
- p90 and p95 respond well to prefetching (reduces queuing) and quantization (reduces kernel time).
- p99 is the hardest: combo lowered it by ~240ms vs baseline but at ~12% higher per-10k cost. Aggressive batching actually increased p99 (more queuing for stragglers) — so batching tradeoff is non-monotonic with tails.

Percentile ladder ASCII sketch (normalised to baseline p50=1.0):
Baseline ladder:  p50=1.0  p90=3.8  p95=5.7  p99=15.2
Prefetch ladder:  p50=0.95 p90=2.9  p95=4.8  p99=13.0
Quant-lite ladder: p50=0.86 p90=3.1 p95=4.9 p99=12.8
Combo ladder:     p50=0.83 p90=2.4 p95=4.0 p99=11.4

Cheap wins vs expensive tails: rule of thumb for this trace
- Improving cache hit by ~10–15% (prefetch) yields ~20–25% improvement in p90/p95 at 5–8% cost delta. Good customer story.
- Reducing kernel time with light quantization yields ~15% p95 improvement and actually lowers cost if latency throughput improves enough to support more packing; but depends on quality/regression risk.
- Any batching increase >20ms wait creates tail exposure for long-running sessions — avoid for p99-sensitive customers.

Short customer-facing script (1–2 bullets for slide):
- "Moving your p90 is relatively cheap: small caching and kernel tweaks reduce p90 by 20–40% for a modest unit cost increase. But p99 reduction typically requires higher capacity or faster kernels — expect non-linear cost."
- "Combo knobs (smart prefetch + conservative quant + moderate batching) sit in the best-effort corner: good p90/p95 wins while keeping cost overhead constrained; we use the same pattern in Dedicated tiers as a standard SLO profile."

Open questions & caveats:
- Quality: quant-lite needs a small eval set; risk of generation artifacts not measured here. Add a quality sweep using our eval harness.
- Prefetch assumptions: we model hitrate; real intent classifiers will vary. Run on a logged trace with actual KV hitrates.
- Single-slab results — need multi-slab and cross-tenant isolation tests to estimate real cost impact for Dedicated.
- Networking/HTTP chunking was not varied; chunking can change observed p99 significantly for long responses.

Next steps (practical):
1) Convert these numbers into an in-console visual: percentile-ladder chart + slider to toggle knobs (goal: interactive story for sales). (Riley pick up)
2) Run quality regression harness for quant-lite across 5 customer prompt sets (Priya). (blocked: evaluation infra ticket INF-3490)
3) Replay 24h production trace with real KV hit fractions and re-run combo mode (Miguel).
4) Draft one-pager for sales explaining cost to move percentiles with 3 recommended knob-sets (this doc -> final). (Asha)

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Consider adding a "cost per millisecond saved at percentile X" metric (dollars per ms at p95/p99) — can make the tradeoff story clearer.
- Might present p99 curves vs provisioned slots rather than raw p99 to show diminishing returns when you add capacity.

References and quick links:
- JIRA-INF-3421: percentile-ladder mini-bench specs
- PR 912: prefetch kernel changes (undoable fallback path documented)
- Confluence: percentile ladder raw data and plots (linked above)

Status: draft — good for internal review and quick spin into a console interactive.
